l1_words.meaning: to intend or plan to do something
to watch (a show, film or event)

pattern_explanation: These Portuguese verbs and adjectives share their spelling with English words because both languages drew on the same Latin roots. Over time the senses diverged, so the look-alike English word does not carry the same meaning.
false_friend_warning: Watch out: the Portuguese verb that means to intend looks almost identical to the English verb pretend, which means to feign something, and the Portuguese adjective that means occasional is easily confused with the English adjective eventual, which means final or ultimate. Translating these words by their spelling produces errors at C2 level.
